sections.name: File setup, CLEAN
sections.title: Imports and text cleanup helper
sections.what: Brings in the phrasing and verification tools, the contest and crew services, and the plan types. Also defines a helper that strips trailing punctuation and spaces from a crew name. Users do not see this directly.
sections.why: Likely reason: people often type a question mark or full stop after a crew name.
sections.watch_out: The helper removes only trailing punctuation, so a name that legitimately ends with one would lose it.

sections.name: plan
sections.title: Routes a question to a plan
sections.what: Turns a question into one of three fixed plans: crew members, crew leader or my crews. Anything else becomes a retrieval plan, and an empty or over-300-character question is unsupported.
sections.why: The comment says only known shapes become database queries.
sections.watch_out: Only exact phrasing matches, so a reworded question falls back to the not-indexed message.

sections.name: findCrewId
sections.title: Finds a crew id by name
sections.what: Looks up the user's crews and returns the id of the one whose name matches, ignoring case, or nothing.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond its name.
sections.watch_out: Only the user's own crews are searched, so crews they are not in cannot be queried.

sections.name: factsFor
sections.title: Collects facts for a structured question
sections.what: Gathers the facts a plan needs: the user's crews and their count, a crew's name, members and count, or the leader and points. Returns an explanation when there is no crew, no members or no scored matches.
sections.why: The comment says the facts are limited to what the asking user may see.
sections.watch_out: A leader with zero points counts as no scored matches, so a crew where everyone is at zero shows as empty.

sections.name: templateFor
sections.title: Fixed sentences for each question
sections.what: Gives the plain wording for each of the three question types, filled from the facts by their ids. This is the fallback wording.
sections.why: The comment says this is deterministic phrasing and the fallback when model phrasing fails.
sections.watch_out: The wording uses fact ids, so renaming an id in the facts step leaves a blank in the sentence.

sections.name: answer
sections.title: Full answer to a question
sections.what: Runs the whole route for one question: plan, then unsupported or retrieval messages, then facts, then phrasing through the verified generation step, returning the sentences and sources.
sections.why: The comment says that with no index yet, the planner says so rather than improvising.
sections.watch_out: The phrasing call uses the fast model tier, and an error from it is not caught here.

summary: Answers simple questions about the user's crews by routing them to fixed database queries, then phrasing the result through a checked template.
purpose: Handles questions such as who is in my crew, who leads, and which crews I am in, without letting a language model choose what to look up.
why: The header says routing is deterministic and the model only phrases results.
how: 1. Trims the question and rejects empty or over-long ones. 2. Matches three fixed question shapes; anything else goes to a retrieval path that says no index exists yet. 3. For a matched question, finds the user's crew by name and loads its facts. 4. Builds a phrasing request with a fixed template and the fact ids. 5. Returns the sentences and their sources.
inputs: A user id, the question text and the current time.
outputs: An answer with the plan, sentences, sources and, when there is nothing to say, an honest message.
risks: Crew names must match exactly, ignoring case, so a typo gives not in a crew. The source label is fixed text rather than a real source record. Phrasing goes through a model call, and an error there is not caught in this file.
debug: If the answer says not in a crew, check the spelling and what listMyCrews returns. If a sentence looks wrong, check the template and the facts. If a question is refused, check its length and whether it matches one of the three patterns.
